built: NO EVENT OR QUEUE MARKS A PLACE AS NEW. 'New' and 'stale' are worked out at read time from three things: the place's name text, atom timestamps and research log rows. The scope SQL is CIS services/acp_contract/segment_research.py:597-609 (_SCOPED_SEGMENTS_SQL). It takes Segments that have an atom of an ACTIVE platform Master (v_active_tour_atoms, owner_scope='platform', NOT deleted). Then segment_research.py:637-651 drops transit and unnamed places using the stored Jev picks. Each row carries atoms_touched = max(coalesce(ta.updated_at, ta.created_at)).

Freshness is stored per (canonical_place TEXT, market, tier) in acp_contract.segment_research_log. The primary key is (canonical_place, market, tier) and tier is volume or serp (db-schema-reference.md:235-245). There is no place id. A place is stale for market M when it has no volume row for M inside cis.seo.research_volume_fresh_days. For US only, it is also stale when it has no serp row inside cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days. Code: _FRESH_LOG_SQL at segment_research.py:611-615 and stale_tiers at :719-728. SERP_MARKET='US' is at segment_research_batch.py:88. stale_tiers is the single definition, shared by the plan, the preview and the guard (research_coverage.py:109-114).

A place counts as 'reatomized', meaning waiting after an atomize (AA-1055, PR #1415, 09/11), when it has no log row at all or when atoms_touched is newer than its newest log row in any market or tier (reatomized_places, segment_research.py:664-678; _NEWEST_RESEARCH_SQL :619-622). Nothing is stored for this. The research_coverage.py:18-20 docstring says it plainly: 'There is no queue table: a research run with scope reatomized ... is that batch'. The API flag is reatomized=true on POST /admin/segment-research/preview and /run (admin_segment_research.py:70-72).

How each path reaches the research scope today. (a) Catalogue import or new tour: S1 ingest, then rewrite, review, Master publish, then the a3_atomize job (enqueued at services/export/handler.py:753). That job runs atomize, then incremental segment_matching. A new place appears as a new atom_segment.canonical_place with no log row, so it is 'reatomized' and stale in every market. (b) Admin re-atomize: admin_atoms.py:641 or the batch consumer at llm_batch/consumers.py:236. The atom upsert sets updated_at=now() only for days whose fingerprint changed (a3_atomize.py:538-586; atomize_day_fingerprint), so the places of those days become 'reatomized'. They are only bought if they are also stale. (c) S1 rewrite of an existing Master: the new version republishes and goes through (b). (d) Tenant T2 rewrite: does NOT atomize (t2_rewrite_job.py:577-591, AA-526/545). It does NOT buy anything (:593-596, AA-646). It only reads seo_context and search_demand (:160-163, :185-193). Tenant atoms are also outside the scope (owner_scope='platform'). So a T2 rewrite never creates a new place. (e) Segment merge or rename: segment_matching.py:872-876 upserts canonical_place = excluded.canonical_place. A renamed place is a new text key with no log row and no place_keyword map, so it shows as 'never researched'.

What AA-646 left in place: an admin-triggered durable job, segment_research (segment_research_job.py:99, concurrency 1). It has a free preview (admin_segment_research.py:121-137) and a run (:140-180). The run refuses when the selection is empty (:155-156), when a run is already active (409), when a budget is exhausted, or when the DFS balance is below the capped estimate (:166-173, re-checked in the job at :110-118). The per-run cap is max_usd = min(payload value, setting cis.spend.segment_research_max_usd_per_run, budget remaining) (job :66-75). That setting defaults to 50 USD with maker_checker approval (migration 407 line 390). narrow_to makes it a HARD per-run stop before every paid post (:78-86). Places that fail or are aborted get no log row and stay stale for the next run (AA-647). After a run, one debounced recompute is enqueued (segment_research.py:773-806). Over 300 Segments, it is deferred to the nightly landing sweep.

Monitoring, which spends nothing: the api ops sampler measures the research stale share once a day (ops_metrics_sampler.py:41-45, 246-253 calls research_coverage.measure). Markets are the DFS markets that active tenants target (TARGET_MARKETS_SQL, research_coverage.py:39-44). The ops check research_stale_share alerts above 20% in any market through the bell plus one e-mail a day (shared/ops_checks.py:110, 415-425). The data coverage 'research' source shows in_scope, allowed, waiting_after_reatomize and stale_<MK> (research_coverage.py:162-179). Tenant360Markets.tsx shows researched and last_researched per tenant market (read only).

Landing sweep (AA-1055): runs on the worker tick every hour (worker.py:168-170, 262-264). It acts only in UTC 17-23, at most once per 20 h, and only when no recompute is active. It re-lands Segments whose questions_computed_at is older than their place's newest research row (landing_sweep.py:20-23, 42-60). It costs nothing itself and is the model for a night-time scheduled tick.

Data that ages, and its windows (AA-1120, CIS 434, merged 16/11 as #1540): (1) Volume: search_demand.retrieved_on per (keyword, market) and log tier 'volume'. Setting cis.seo.research_volume_fresh_days, default 365, range 30-730. (2) SERP (PAA, related searches, organic domains): search_demand.paa_retrieved_on plus log tier 'serp'. Bought ONCE per place in US/English only. Setting cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days, default 365, range 30-730. (3) Paid queued task recovery: cis.seo.dfs_queue_recover_days, default 7. Sources: research_settings.py:11-16; migration 434 lines 18-20 and 54-56; research_cache.py:98-117 reads them per run. NOTE: all three are seeded with approval 'single', not maker_checker. (4) The place keyword map (acp_contract.place_keyword) never expires. It is proposed again only when PROMPT_VERSION changes (the hash of the propose prompt, segment_research_batch.py:127) or when needs_requalify is true (:348-373). (5) Tour-level seo_context (S1, where tour PAA comes from) is reused for S1_SEO_REUSE_DAYS=180, an env var (s1_prefetch.py:40), plus a 7-day Redis TTL that is a code literal (handler.py:38). It is refreshed only when a tour is rewritten by S1.
missing: No scheduled research run of any kind. No worker tick, sampler part or job ever calls run_segment_research with dry_run=False. 'Reatomized' places wait until someone calls POST /admin/segment-research/run. No admin frontend page calls /admin/segment-research/* (grep of frontend/app and frontend/lib finds only the read-only Tenant360Markets coverage). So today 'admin-triggered' means an API call with the admin secret.

No monthly DFS cap can be set. shared.spend_budget has a per_month_usd column (CIS 340), but PUT /admin/budgets refuses it on any non-llm provider row ('a month cap applies to an llm (central) row only', admin_budgets.py:64-65). cost_guard.RunBudget only enforces per_run and per_day (shared/cost_guard.py:151-209). The daily DFS cap is alert-only (AA-1055 export, comment of 09/11). So the S273 proposal of 5 USD/month (design.vi.md:166, AA-1055 export :84) cannot be enforced today. The only hard stop is per run.

Under a cap, new places are not bought first. _plan sorts the stale places by name (segment_research.py:763) and select_within_usd takes the cheapest-fitting PREFIX (segment_research_batch.py:284-298). A capped automatic run would always buy 'A...' places first and could starve 'Z...' places and new places. There is no ordering by never-researched first, oldest researched_at, tenant-targeted market, or Segment rank or recurrence.

No rolling refresh. A place only becomes stale AFTER its window ends. Nothing refreshes it early (the S273 '1/12 of the oldest catalogue per month' idea, design.vi.md:166, is not built). Nearly all log rows were written 08-16/11/2026 (S273-S282 runs). With today's 365/365 windows the whole scope (~5,877 places x 6 markets) goes stale at the same time, around 08-16/11/2027. With 180-day windows that would happen around May 2027. The S273 estimate for a full re-buy is about 10.17 USD volume plus about 11.32 USD PAA for 6 markets (design.vi.md:220-221). The 25/09 incident was exactly a large burst run.

Place identity is free text. A rename or merge (segment_matching.py:876) does not carry the research log or the keyword map to the new name. The S273 design promised that a rename carries the map over through the Segment alias (design.vi.md:155); it is not built (no place_keyword or segment_research_log reference in segment_matching or the place dedupe/relocate jobs). The volume store softens this: if the plain keyword is unchanged, the volume is a free cache hit. The map is still proposed again by the LLM, and the place counts as 'never researched'.

A new ACTIVITY at a place that is already fresh gets no new keywords. The map is proposed once from the actions present at that moment (_listing_line, up to 6 actions, segment_research_batch.py:525-532). A fresh place is reused until its window ends (reusable_keywords :348-360). A new tour that adds 'X cooking class' to a known place therefore has its new Segment ranked only on the place's old keywords.

The 'reatomized' signal is noisy and is not a 'new place' signal. Any re-atomized day updates updated_at, so places that are still fresh are flagged too. On 09/11, 4 of 4 places were 'reatomized' and only 2 were stale (AA-1055 export :160-162). This is harmless because the plan only buys stale tiers. A reliable 'new place' test is 'no segment_research_log row for this canonical_place', or a rename alias.

A new mapped market has no gate. When a tenant starts targeting a mapped market that no other tenant targets (for example a first DE agency), every place becomes stale in that market at once. TARGET_MARKETS_SQL picks this up the next day. An automatic job must treat 'market activation' (about 1.7 USD volume per market, AA-1055 export :87) as its own capped, approved batch, not as part of the monthly top-up.

Several research values are hard-coded or set only by env var, which breaks the S279 rule that every threshold is a setting. They are: STALE_SHARE_LIMIT=0.20 and CHECK_EVERY_S=86400 (research_coverage.py:32-33); IMMEDIATE_RECOMPUTE_MAX_SEGMENTS=300 (segment_research.py:634); landing sweep SWEEP_UTC_HOURS / MIN_GAP_H / MAX_SEGMENTS plus env LANDING_SWEEP (landing_sweep.py:34-40); S1_SEO_REUSE_DAYS env 180 (s1_prefetch.py:40); the Redis SEO TTL of 7 days (handler.py:38). The freshness windows are settings, but with 'single' approval (no maker-checker).
SERP and PAA freshness is tracked only for US. A UK/AU/DE agency's PAA comes from the one US/English SERP per place. No per-market SERP tier exists to age.
facts: CIS origin/main at bc5c0bd49 (16/11). Research cache AA-1120 merged as #1540 (53e016464, 16/11). Stale guard and reatomized scope merged as #1415 (116179b3c, 09/11).

segment_research_log has about 41,421 rows, PK (canonical_place, market, tier), tier CHECK in ('volume','serp'). atom_segment has created_at only (no updated_at). search_demand has about 105,092 rows with retrieved_on (volume) and paa_retrieved_on (SERP). Source: db-schema-reference.md, verified 16/11 06:56 UTC, CIS 434.

The per-run cap is setting cis.spend.segment_research_max_usd_per_run, default 50 USD, range 1-200, maker_checker (migration 407:390). The job narrows the DFS budget's per-run cap to max_usd and makes it a hard stop (segment_research_job.py:78-86).

There are three proven patterns for a scheduled tick. (1) Worker tick with a window, a minimum gap measured by looking for its own job row in shared.job, and a skip while a related job is active: landing_sweep.py:98-119. (2) The api ops sampler enqueues with a per-period idempotency key: report chain kpi_snapshot_daily:<day>, report_jobs.py:17. (3) A job that requeues itself with run_after: place_relocate_job.py:252.

segment_research is not deploy_gate_exempt (default in shared/jobs/registry.py:96) and expected_seconds=3600. An automatic run therefore blocks backend deploys while it runs (DM-11.4) and should run in the night window, like the landing sweep (UTC 17-23).

The S273 design (docs/audits/2026-11-08-S273-session/dfs-cost-audit/design.vi.md §5, lines 151-168) proposes: volume 365 days, because Google Ads volume is a 12-month average and refreshing it twice a year buys almost nothing new; PAA 365 days; a monthly plan on the 1st with new places plus about 1/12 of the oldest; a cap of 5 USD/month; no automatic spending (approve-by-click). The estimated steady state is about 2.9 USD/month, or about 1.1 USD/month for new places only.
AA-1055 export (:84) recorded the pending idea of a 5 USD/month cap for incremental research plus a full refresh every 6 months. The tech lead has now asked for the automatic version (item 2).

Cost of the automatic path at today's rates (S273 measurements): new places cost about 0.54 USD per month for volume (1 task per market x 6 x 0.09), about 0.46 USD for SERP (300 x 0.773 x 0.002) and about 0.08 USD for LLM. The '300 new places/month' figure is an assumption that was never measured. Today's live top-up was DFS 0.64 plus LLM 0.012 USD.
triggers.recommendation:
Build one automatic job for this, `segment_research_auto`. Do not add a second way to measure staleness. Steps:

(1) Trigger. Add a part to the api ops sampler or the worker tick that follows the landing-sweep pattern. It runs only in the night window. It enqueues `segment_research` with created_by 'system:auto' and idempotency key `segment_research:auto:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. It runs at most once per N days and is skipped while any segment_research job is queued or running. N, the window and an on/off switch become new settings with maker_checker approval:
- cis.seo.research_auto_enabled (default off until the tech lead switches it on)
- cis.seo.research_auto_every_days (default 30, or 7 for new places only)
- cis.seo.research_auto_utc_hours

(2) Selection. Reuse run_segment_research with the markets returned by research_coverage.target_markets, so only markets that active tenants target are bought. Add a priority order before select_within_usd: places never researched come first, then places stale in a targeted market, then the oldest researched_at. A market that just became targeted, with every place stale in it, is left out of the automatic run and reported as its own batch with its price.

(3) Rolling refresh instead of a 6-month cliff. Add a setting cis.seo.research_refresh_ahead_days so that each automatic run also refreshes the oldest slice, about 1/12 per month, before it expires. Keep volume at 365 days, since Google volume is a 12-month average and a 6-month volume refresh buys almost nothing. If the tech lead wants newer questions, lower only cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days to 180. That is a settings change, no code. It should become maker_checker, like the other spend-affecting keys.

(4) Hard monthly cap. Allow per_month_usd on the DFS `job:segment_research` row, or add a setting cis.spend.segment_research_auto_max_usd_per_month (default 5). Teach cost_guard.RunBudget to check the UTC-month DFS spend (dfs_call_log) plus LLM spend before every paid post. Pass the remaining month budget as max_usd, so narrow_to stops the run at the cap. An exhausted month cap means 'skipped: cap reached', never a partial overspend.

(5) Ledger and UI. Add an admin card showing the next run, the last automatic run (places bought, DFS and LLM USD from the job's cost and dfs_call_log), the month spend against the cap, places waiting, and the switch. Add a Preview/Run page for the existing API, which has none today.

(6) Fix the identity gaps. On a Segment rename or merge, copy the place_keyword map and the segment_research_log rows from the old canonical_place to the new one. Mark the map for a new proposal when a place gains an action that was not in its map's actions.

(7) Move the hard-coded values into the Settings registry: STALE_SHARE_LIMIT, IMMEDIATE_RECOMPUTE_MAX_SEGMENTS, the landing sweep hours, gap and maximum, S1_SEO_REUSE_DAYS and the Redis SEO TTL.

Detection only works once the atoms exist. A new tour's places can only be researched after Master publish and A3 atomize, so its S1 rewrite still runs before research. Tour-level PAA (item 1) is a separate path, seo_context, with its own 180-day env window.

agency.recommendation:
To make the system ready to sell to agencies on the market side, here is what to do, in order.

(1) Keep Brand Identity Target Markets as the only market an agency sets. Make planning markets (acp_shared.tenant_config.markets) derive from it, or show as read-only next to it, so the two lists cannot disagree.

(2) Replace the 8 hard-coded market lists with one admin Settings registry entry per market, changed with maker-checker. Each entry holds: code, DFS location code, language, status (researched | proxy | off), proxy_of, and alias words. SERP_MARKET and STALE_SHARE_LIMIT become settings too. Enabling a market sets unmapped_market_requests.resolved_at for that country.

(3) Unsupported market policy, with two steps:
- Step 1, $0 and at once: a proxy, labelled for admin only. CA->US, NZ->AU, SG/HK/AE->UK (SA->UK too, or off, since Saudi search is mostly Arabic). The portal note changes from 'uses US' to 'uses UK search data'.
- Step 2: when a paying agency declares an English-searching market (SG, HK, AE, CA, NZ), admin turns it to 'researched'. The next monthly research plan includes it under the monthly cap (about 1 USD per full volume pass on the Standard queue, measured S274), and the proxy stops.
Never buy for a market no active agency declares.

(4) Finish the S273 agency-side reads:
- T2 reads all of the agency's markets (max volume, ties go to the first declared market) and takes PAA from the US SERP. This fixes the UK/AU/DE agencies that probably get no PAA today.
- T8 and T9 read search_demand for the agency's markets, falling back to seo_context.

Khái niệm 'cũ' vẫn chỉ có một định nghĩa (stale_tiers). Mỗi ngày sampler đếm số chỗ mới, chỗ cũ, chỗ sắp hết hạn theo từng thị trường. Mỗi đêm tick 'research_auto' quyết có chạy hay không.

Kiểm hàng tháng chạy thế nào: có 2 nhịp. (a) Đợt chỗ mới: xét mỗi đêm, chỉ chạy khi có từ 20 chỗ mới trở lên hoặc chỗ mới cũ nhất đã chờ quá 7 ngày, nên mỗi tour mới có dữ liệu trong khoảng 1 đến 7 ngày. (b) Đợt làm mới: 30 ngày một lần, mua lại chỗ đã quá hạn, rồi tới chỗ sẽ hết hạn trong 180 ngày tới (mỗi lượt tối đa 17% phạm vi). Nhờ vậy khối dữ liệu mua 08–16/11/2026 không hết hạn cùng một lúc vào 11/2027. Thứ tự trong mỗi lượt: chỗ chưa từng nghiên cứu, rồi chỗ cũ nhất, rồi chỗ nhiều tour dùng nhất.

Tiền và chặn: mỗi lượt tự động tối đa 3 USD. Mỗi tháng tối đa 5 USD, tính cả DFS lẫn LLM và cả lượt chạy tay. Trước mỗi lần gửi request trả tiền đều kiểm phần trần còn lại, hết thì dừng cứng. Khi chạm trần, chạy lỗi, hoặc chỗ mới chờ quá 14 ngày thì có chuông, và một e-mail mỗi ngày. Lượt tự động mặc định TẮT; anh bật bằng khoá cis.seo.research_auto_enabled.

Khi có tour mới: S1 viết lại, rồi review, rồi publish Master, rồi atomize. Chỗ mới được xếp vào danh sách chờ (không mua ngay) và đêm sau, hoặc trong vòng 7 ngày, được mua trong giới hạn trần. Sau đó recompute, và Slate cùng T2 thấy nhu cầu tìm kiếm. Trước khi có số, nội dung vẫn viết bình thường, chỉ không có tín hiệu nhu cầu như hiện nay.

Khi viết lại tour: AA viết lại (S1) thì chỉ những ngày có thay đổi được atomize lại. Chỗ còn mới không bị mua lại. Chỗ mới thì vào danh sách chờ. Nếu một chỗ có thêm hoạt động mới (ví dụ thêm lớp nấu ăn), bộ từ khoá của chỗ đó được đề xuất lại bằng LLM; volume của các từ khoá cũ lấy lại từ cache nên miễn phí. Đổi tên hoặc gộp địa điểm thì chép log và bộ từ khoá sang tên mới, không mua lại. Đại lý viết lại (T2) thì $0: chỉ đọc cache, không tạo chỗ mới, không mua.

Tìm theo brand đại lý: đề xuất KHÔNG làm. Đại lý nhỏ gần như không ai tìm theo tên, nên không giúp chọn nội dung. Thứ đáng mua là nhu cầu theo điểm đến và hoạt động ở thị trường của đại lý, và hệ thống đã làm việc này. Brand chỉ dùng làm đầu vào cho người viết. Thêm lớp lọc $0: T9 và keyword_fit loại các từ khoá chứa tên công ty tour khác hoặc tên chính đại lý.

Thị trường của đại lý: nghiên cứu phủ hợp của các thị trường 'thật' mà các đại lý đang hoạt động khai, cộng với thị trường mặc định của nền tảng (US). Đại lý thêm một thị trường thật mà chưa ai dùng thì lượt tự động đêm sau mua cho thị trường đó, tối đa 1,5 USD, nằm trong trần tháng. Trong lúc chờ, nội dung dùng các thị trường khác của đại lý và portal ghi rõ điều này. Thị trường proxy thì đọc số của thị trường gốc, $0.

Thị trường mới: dữ liệu thật của DataForSEO có cho cả 6 nước (CA 2124, NZ 2554, SG 2702, AE 2784, HK 2344, SA 2682; HK và SA cần kiểm lại bằng endpoint locations miễn phí). Đề xuất làm lai: đưa danh sách thị trường vào một registry sửa trong admin (không phải sửa code), mặc định SG/HK/AE/SA dùng UK, CA dùng US, NZ dùng AU, có nhãn 'proxy'. Khi đại lý trả tiền khai thị trường đó, admin bấm 'nâng lên dữ liệu thật'. Lần mua đầu khoảng 1 USD mỗi thị trường, làm mới khoảng 0,08 USD mỗi thị trường mỗi tháng.

PAA cấp tour cho 258 tour: không mua lại SERP cũ (các SERP đó không có ô PAA, mua lại cũng rỗng, và code còn trả lại bản rỗng miễn phí). Bước 1 ($0): lấy PAA tiếng Anh từ kho search_demand theo địa điểm của tour (cả tên trong tiêu đề lẫn địa điểm của atom). Bước 2: tour nào vẫn rỗng thì mua top-up theo '<địa điểm> <nước>', khoảng 0,0023 USD mỗi tour, tối đa khoảng 0,6 USD. Sau đó PAA tự làm mới theo kho địa điểm (365 ngày). Thời hạn dùng lại 180 ngày và TTL Redis chuyển thành khoá Settings.

# Search-demand data always ready to sell — design (S282, 16/11/2026)

Read-only design. CIS origin/main bc5c0bd49, Partner origin/main 900566ab, root docs. No AWS, DFS, LLM or DB calls. Next free CIS migration number: 435.

## 0. Principles
- One definition of "stale". `segment_research.stale_tiers` stays the only rule, used by the plan, the preview, the guard and the new auto job. "New place" = a canonical_place in scope with **no** `acp_contract.segment_research_log` row. Rows are never pre-computed into a queue table: the "queue" is the read-time selection (research_coverage.py:18-20 already says so).
- Events queue; only the scheduled job buys. Atomize, rewrite, rename, a tenant market change and a market promotion all change what the next selection returns. None of them calls DataForSEO (AA-646 holds).
- Every value is a Settings registry key (shared.setting_definition, CIS 407 pattern). Spend-affecting keys use maker_checker. Readers name keys through a constants module, like research_settings.py.
- Every automatic purchase has a per-run cap, a calendar-month cap and a hard stop before each paid post. An exhausted cap means "skipped: cap reached", never a partial overspend. The ledger is shared.dfs_call_log + shared.llm_call_log (stage `segment_research`) + the shared.job row (created_by `system:auto`).

## A. Places: detection, triggers, scheduled job, caps, alerts, admin

### A1. Detection (built + small fixes)
| Path | What happens | Buys? |
|---|---|---|
| New AA tour: S1 ingest → rewrite → review → Master publish → `a3_atomize` (export/handler.py:753) → incremental segment_matching | each new place = new `atom_segment.canonical_place` with no log row → **new**, stale in every targeted market | No. Queued implicitly; the next auto run buys it |
| AA re-atomize / S1 rewrite of an existing Master | only days whose fingerprint changed get updated_at=now (a3_atomize.py:538-586) → "reatomized". Fresh places stay fresh | Only the tiers that are really stale |
| New activity at a known fresh place (**new**) | after segment_matching, compare the place's live actions to the actions its `place_keyword` map was proposed from. If a new action exists → set `needs_requalify=true` | LLM re-propose only (~$0.0001/place). Volumes for unchanged keywords come free from the AA-1120 cache. New keywords cost one volume task share |
| Segment rename / merge (segment_matching.py:872-876) (**new**) | copy the `segment_research_log` rows + `place_keyword` map from the old canonical_place to the new one (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) in the same transaction as the rename | No |
| Tenant T2 rewrite | no atomize, tenant atoms are out of scope (owner_scope='platform'), reads the cache only (t2_rewrite_job.py:151-213) | Never |
| Agency adds a **real** market (Brand tab) | TARGET_MARKETS_SQL picks it up. Every place becomes stale in that market → treated as a **market activation** batch (A3) | Inside its own activation cap |
| Agency adds a proxy / unknown market | proxy read, unmapped_market_requests row | Never |

The noisy "reatomized" signal stays for the preview and coverage only. The auto job uses "never researched" and "stale tier".

### A2. Scheduled job `research_auto` (worker tick, landing-sweep pattern)
- New module `services/acp_contract/research_auto.py`, called from the worker tick (worker.py next to landing_sweep). Each tick:
  1. If `cis.seo.research_auto_enabled` is false → return `disabled`.
  2. If the UTC hour is outside [`window_start_utc`, `window_end_utc`) → return.
  3. If any `segment_research` job is queued or running, or a recompute is active → skip (same check as landing_sweep.py:98-119).
  4. Measure the pending selection (free, bounded, research_coverage + one new query): `new` (places with no log row, with oldest first_seen = min atom created_at), `stale` per market, `refresh_ahead` per market, `activation` markets.
  5. Decide the run type:
     - **New-places run**: new ≥ `research_auto_new_min_places`, OR the oldest new place has waited ≥ `research_auto_new_max_wait_days`. At most one per UTC day.
     - **Refresh run**: the last automatic refresh run is older than `research_auto_refresh_every_days`.
     - Neither → return `nothing_due`.
  6. Compute the money left: `month_left = month_cap − spend_this_UTC_month(segment_research, DFS + LLM, manual + auto)`. `max_usd = min(auto per-run cap, month_left, cis.spend.segment_research_max_usd_per_run, budget remaining)`. If max_usd is below `research_auto_min_run_usd` → record a `skipped_cap` row in the tick result and raise the ops check; do not enqueue.
  7. Enqueue `segment_research` with payload {scope: 'auto_new' | 'auto_refresh', markets: target real markets, max_usd, priority: true}, created_by `system:auto`, idempotency key `segment_research:auto:<kind>:<YYYY-MM-DD>`. The job already has concurrency 1, the balance gate, narrow_to as a hard per-post stop and AA-647 (failed places stay stale).
- Runs in the night window so it never collides with daytime deploys (segment_research is not deploy_gate_exempt).

### A3. Selection order (change in `segment_research._plan` + `segment_research_batch.select_within_usd`)
Today the plan sorts by name and takes the cheapest prefix (segment_research.py:763, batch :284-298). A capped run would starve Z-places and new places. New ordering, used by manual runs too:
1. Never-researched places (all target real markets), most active platform tours first, then oldest first_seen.
2. Stale tiers in target real markets, oldest researched_at first, ties broken by the number of active tours using the place.
3. Refresh run only: refresh-ahead tiers whose window ends within `research_refresh_ahead_days`, oldest first, at most `research_refresh_max_share_pct` of the scope per run.
4. Market activation: a real market that is newly targeted (more than `research_auto_activation_stale_pct` of its scope stale) is bought in its own sub-batch capped at `research_auto_market_activation_max_usd`, still inside the month cap. If the activation cap is 0, the market only shows in the panel with its preview price and waits for a manual run.
select_within_usd keeps whole places (volume + SERP tiers together) and walks this order until the next place does not fit.

### A4. Hard monthly cap (change in cost_guard)
- shared/cost_guard.py RunBudget gains `month_cap_usd` + `month_spent_usd` (one SUM over dfs_call_log and llm_call_log for stage segment_research and the current UTC month, re-read before every paid post). The job passes the smaller of the run cap and the month remainder to narrow_to. Concurrency 1 means there are no races.
- No change to PUT /admin/budgets: the month cap is a setting, not a spend_budget per_month_usd row (that row stays llm-only, admin_budgets.py:64-65).

### A5. Alerts (shared/ops_checks.py, bell once per 20 h + one e-mail a day, existing mechanism)
- `research_auto_failed`: the last auto job failed or was aborted.
- `research_auto_capped`: the run was skipped or stopped at the run or month cap with places still pending (message: pending count + price of the rest).
- `research_new_waiting`: the oldest new place has waited longer than `cis.ops.research_new_wait_alert_days`.
- `research_month_spend`: month spend ≥ `cis.ops.research_month_warn_pct` of the month cap.
- `research_stale_share` (exists): limit becomes a setting.

### A6. Admin panel (CIS frontend, `/admin/seo-intelligence`, new "Research" tab; API `GET /admin/segment-research/status`)
- Auto switch (links to the Settings key), next eligible run (window + rule that will fire), last 10 runs (manual + auto: kind, places bought per market, DFS USD, LLM USD, status, stop reason), month spend vs month cap (bar), the per-run cap.
- Pending: new places (count, oldest wait, list with place, country, tours, first seen), stale per market, refresh-ahead per market, activation markets with their preview price.
- Buttons: Preview (existing free POST /preview) and Run (existing POST /run, admin role, its own caps). Today no page calls these routes.
- The data coverage "research" row stays as it is.

### A7. Settings registry keys (new unless marked)
| Key | Type | Default | Bounds | Approval |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| cis.seo.research_auto_enabled | bool | false | — | maker_checker |
| cis.seo.research_auto_window_start_utc | int | 17 | 0-23 | single |
| cis.seo.research_auto_window_end_utc | int | 23 | 1-24 | single |
| cis.seo.research_auto_new_min_places | int | 20 | 1-5000 | single |
| cis.seo.research_auto_new_max_wait_days | int | 7 | 1-60 | single |
| cis.seo.research_auto_refresh_every_days | int | 30 | 7-120 | maker_checker |
| cis.seo.research_refresh_ahead_days | int | 180 | 0-365 | maker_checker |
| cis.seo.research_refresh_max_share_pct | pct | 17 | 0-100 | maker_checker |
| cis.seo.research_auto_activation_stale_pct | pct | 50 | 10-100 | single |
| cis.spend.research_auto_market_activation_max_usd | usd | 1.5 | 0-10 | maker_checker |
| cis.spend.research_auto_max_usd_per_run | usd | 3 | 0.1-50 | maker_checker |
| cis.spend.research_max_usd_per_month | usd | 5 | 0-100 | maker_checker |
| cis.spend.research_auto_min_run_usd | usd | 0.05 | 0-5 | single |
| cis.ops.research_new_wait_alert_days | int | 14 | 1-90 | single |
| cis.ops.research_month_warn_pct | pct | 80 | 10-100 | single |
| cis.ops.research_stale_share_limit_pct (was STALE_SHARE_LIMIT) | pct | 20 | 1-100 | single |
| cis.ops.research_check_every_s (was CHECK_EVERY_S) | duration_s | 86400 | 3600-604800 | single |
| cis.recompute.immediate_max_segments (was IMMEDIATE_RECOMPUTE_MAX_SEGMENTS) | int | 300 | 10-5000 | single |
| cis.recompute.landing_sweep_enabled (env LANDING_SWEEP kept as env_override) | bool | true | — | single |
| cis.recompute.landing_sweep_window_start_utc / _end_utc | int | 17 / 23 | 0-24 | single |
| cis.recompute.landing_sweep_min_gap_h | int | 20 | 1-168 | single |
| cis.recompute.landing_sweep_max_segments | int | 5000 | 100-50000 | single |
| cis.seo.research_volume_fresh_days (exists) | int | 365 | 30-730 | single → **maker_checker** |
| cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days (exists) | int | 365 | 30-730 | single → **maker_checker** |
| cis.spend.segment_research_max_usd_per_run (exists) | usd | 50 | 1-200 | maker_checker |
Keep volume at 365 days: Google Ads volume is a 12-month average. If fresher questions are wanted, lower only the SERP window, and that is a settings change.

### A8. Steady-state cost (S273 measurements; the new-place rate is an assumption)
New places about 1 USD/month (volume 0.54 + SERP 0.46 + LLM 0.08 at about 300 places/month). Rolling refresh from about May 2027 about 1.8-3.6 USD/month (full re-buy about 21.5 USD/year for 6 markets). Inside 5 USD/month. Before May 2027 the refresh run buys almost nothing.

## B. Agency markets and brand

### B1. Research market set
`research markets = {real markets declared by active tenants} ∪ cis.seo.platform_default_markets (list, default ["US"], maker_checker)`. Proxy and off markets are never bought. A tenant with no declared market counts as the platform default (today: US). Scope stays platform places only: agencies adopt AA tours, so a new agency adds markets, never places.

### B2. One market list per agency
The Brand Identity Target Markets (tenant_brand_rules.target_markets → shared.tenant_seo_config.target_market) is the only place an agency sets markets. `acp_shared.tenant_config.markets` (planning N4-N6, default ['US']) is derived from it on save and shown read-only on the Planning tab. Tenant360 keeps both columns until the derive ships.

### B3. When an agency adds a market
- Real market already researched: no cost, T2/Slate use it at once.
- Real market not yet researched by anyone (first DE agency): it joins the research set the next day, and the auto run buys it as an activation sub-batch (≤ 1.5 USD, inside the month cap). Until then, T2 and Slate use the agency's other real markets, or its proxy. The portal note says "<market>: search data is being prepared; your content uses <X> data until then".
- Proxy market (SG→UK etc.): $0. Reads use proxy_of data. Portal note: "Singapore uses UK search data". Admin sees "proxy" in Tenant360, the Slate reason and the unmapped queue.
- Unknown text: kept as today ('Not recognised'). The unmapped request row is written. The admin can add a registry row.

### B4. Reads fixed to be per agency market
- T2: read all of the agency's real or proxy-resolved markets (MAX volume, ties go to the first declared market). Take PAA from the US/en SERP rows for the same places (SERP is US once per place by design). Today a UK-first agency's T2 cache hit probably replaces seo_context with volume-only rows, so it gets no PAA (inferred from code, check live with a $0 SELECT in the slice). Record `seo_markets_used` in job.result.
- T8 angles / T9 blog keyword: read search_demand for the agency's markets, falling back to seo_context (US). Record the market used.

### B5. Brand-name search: do not do it
A small agency's brand gets about zero search volume. Buying it adds cost and never changes which tours or topics to write. What is searched instead: destination × activity demand in the agency's markets (place keyword maps: '<place> <activity>', '<country> tour', PAA for places), which already drives the Slate, T2 and T9. Brand stays a writer input (T2 CLIENT BRAND, T9 BRAND line, SEO title variant). Add one $0 guard: T9 `choose_keyword` gets the T2 rule (every content word of the keyword must appear in the source), plus a blocked-terms list `cis.seo.keyword_blocked_terms` (list, default = the known operator names seen in related searches, single approval). The agency's own brand name is excluded from DFS keyword candidates.

## C. New markets: real vs proxy, market registry

### C1. Market registry, data not code
New setting `cis.seo.market_registry` (value_type json, maker_checker, compiled default = today's values). The reader validates it with a pydantic schema and keeps last-good on a bad value. One entry per market:
`{code, dfs_location_code, volume_language ('en'), status: real|proxy|off, proxy_of, rank, aliases[], blog_min_demand (null = global bar), serp: bool}`.
Seed: US 2840 real (serp=true), UK 2826, AU 2036, DE 2276, FR 2250, NL 2528 real; CA 2124 proxy→US; NZ 2554 proxy→AU; SG 2702, HK 2344, AE 2784, SA 2682 proxy→UK (SA also allowed 'off', because Saudi search is mostly Arabic).
It replaces: seed_builder.DFS_LOCATION_MAP / MARKET_RANK / _DEFAULT_MARKET, brand_intake/markets.SUPPORTED and its aliases, admin_dashboard.MARKETS, admin_seo._MARKETS, real_questions._MARKET_ORDER, segment_research_batch.SERP_MARKET/SERP_LANGUAGE (= entries with serp=true), the admin_llm_ops location-name table and the market check of admin_segment_research.py:74-81. One module `services/seo_intelligence/market_registry.py` exposes `real_markets()`, `resolve(code) -> (data_market, is_proxy)`, `location_code(code)` and `aliases()`.
Resolution of an agency market: real → itself; proxy → proxy_of (labelled); off/unknown → the agency's first real market, else the platform default.
Recompute scores real markets only. A proxy reads its proxy_of ranking, so proxies add no recompute load.

### C2. Promote a market (admin)
On `/admin/llm-ops/unmapped-market-requests`, a "Promote to real" action proposes a registry change (maker-checker). On approval, `resolved_at` is set for that country's requests. The next auto run buys the market as an activation sub-batch. "Back to proxy" is the reverse change, and its data is kept.

### C3. Real vs proxy, recommendation
- Locations exist for all 6 (HK 2344 / SA 2682 are from public Google Ads lists: confirm with the free `/v3/keywords_data/google_ads/locations` call before seeding).
- A proxy costs $0, but its absolute demand is inflated about 5-10x (UK 67M people vs SG 6M). Ranking between places is broadly usable, absolute bars are not, so the proxy label is mandatory.
- Real data costs about 1 USD per market for the first full volume pass (S274 R2: 0.96 USD per market for about 5,558 places, Standard queue), then about 0.08 USD per market per month rolling. SERP stays US once per place.
- Recommendation: hybrid. Every new market starts as a proxy at $0. Promote to real when a paying agency declares it: CA, NZ, SG first. Promote AE, SA, HK only if a trial hit rate (share of keywords with volume > 0) clears `cis.seo.market_min_hit_rate_pct` (default 25). Before small real markets go live, the Blog bar must be relative per market (registry `blog_min_demand`, or a relative rule), because the absolute 1,000 bar gives SG/NZ/HK almost no Blog topics (S273 decision 6).
- Never buy a market that no active agency declares.

## D. Tour-level PAA (the 258) and freshness
- Facts: tour PAA = silver_aa_internal.seo_context.people_also_ask, one US row per tour. All 892 tours have a row, and 258 have an empty PAA array. Re-running the S1 prefetch buys nothing (fresh 180 days until about April 2027), and a forced re-buy would most likely return no PAA box again.
- D1. Free derive (new $0 job kind `tour_paa_from_store`, admin route `POST /admin/s1/tour-paa/preview|run`). For each tour with empty PAA it collects English PAA from acp_contract.search_demand for its title places AND its atom places (v_active_tour_atoms), from any market, using real_questions.PlacePaaSource filters (off-meaning, English, dedupe), with at most `cis.seo.tour_paa_max` questions. It writes only when the list is empty and never overwrites a bought list. Provenance: new columns `paa_source` ('serp'|'store'|'topup') + `paa_filled_at` (migration 437, expand). The preview returns: would fill N, still empty M, $0.
- D2. Paid top-up for the rest: question_topup on the tour's main place ('<place> <country>', click depth 2, about 0.0023 USD each) as a job behind an admin route with a preview, under the existing maker-checker cap cis.spend.question_topup_cap_usd (3 USD). Upper bound: 258 × 0.0023 ≈ 0.60 USD.
- D3. Keep it fresh. `fresh_tour_ids` / `load_fresh` / `seed_serps` treat an empty PAA list as "PAA tier missing", so they never reuse []. After every research run that wrote SERP rows, the job enqueues `tour_paa_from_store` ($0) for tours whose PAA is empty or whose `paa_source='store'` is older than `cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days`. New and rewritten tours therefore get PAA from the monthly place research, and S1 buys a live SERP only when the store has nothing (the full S1-stops-buying switch is S273 PR 3, later).
- D4. critics.verdict: APPROVE WITH REQUIRED CHANGES (cost-safety lens). The shape is right: events only change the selection, one scheduled job buys, it runs at most once a day per kind (shared.job.idempotency_key is unique for good, queue.py:112-124), and proxies are $0. But as written, the monthly cap would not hold in code. Five defects can let spending pass a cap or repeat without a stop: (1) the ledger SUM uses the wrong stage names, so it would read about $0; (2) the month cap narrows only DFS; LLM and Jev spend sit outside it; (3) every retry or deploy release starts a new per-run budget, and log writes are fire-and-forget; (4) D3 turns an empty PAA list into a loop of repeat purchases; (5) B3 market activation is a tenant action that sets off a platform-wide buy. That is the 25/09 shape, only capped, and lead, trial and demo tenants count towards it today. Fix C1-C6 before S2/S3/S6 merge. C7-C14 are bounded but should go into the same slices. Verified on CIS origin/main bc5c0bd49, read-only.
corrections: C1 (blocker, S2) The month-cap ledger filter is wrong. Research does not write stage 'segment_research'. Its DFS rows carry stage 'a3_search_demand': DataForSEOClient(budget=dfs_budget, stage=rb.RESEARCH_STAGE) at segment_research.py:906, with RESEARCH_STAGE='a3_search_demand' at segment_research_batch.py:90. Its own LLM ledger rows are also 'a3_search_demand' (segment_research_batch.py:489-490, segment_research.py:507). The gateway request stage is 'segment_research_batch' (:81). Jev asks use JEV_STAGE='a3_research' (:80, decide at :415 and :847). A SUM WHERE stage='segment_research' would read about $0 and the 5 USD cap would never stop anything. Fix: measure by job, not by stage, with the existing pattern _KIND_DAY_SPEND_SQL (shared/cost_guard.py, the shared.job join): SUM(dfs_call_log.cost_usd) + SUM(llm_call_log.cost_usd) over rows JOIN shared.job j ON j.id = job_id WHERE j.kind='segment_research' AND created_at >= UTC month start. This covers manual and auto runs plus the LLM, gateway and Jev rows. dfs_call_log has job_id with index idx_dfs_call_log_job (db-schema-reference.md:11903-11929). The ledger read must fail closed: an unreadable SUM means 'refuse', never 0. Add a test that a fake run's DFS + LLM + Jev rows all count.

C2 (blocker, S2) Make the month remainder one shared counter for every paid axis. Today max_usd and narrow_to only touch the DFS RunBudget (segment_research_job.py:66-86, 106-107). The LLM budget is a separate 'bedrock' job:segment_research row (SAFE_DEFAULTS 2 USD per run, cost_guard.py:41-43), checked only at segment_research.py:487 and segment_research_batch.py:472. Jev decide() calls are not checked against any run budget. With the design's 'month_left → narrow_to', DFS could take the whole month remainder and LLM + Jev could still spend on top. Fix: build a MonthBudget object at job start = month cap − ledger month spend (C1). dfs_budget.check, llm_budget.check and the Jev path each call it before posting and charge it after. Reserve the LLM propose estimate before computing the DFS max_usd for select_within_usd (segment_research_batch.py:284-298 prices DFS only).

C3 (blocker, S2) A per-run cap resets on every attempt. segment_research is max_attempts=2 (segment_research_job.py:99). Generic exceptions are retried (worker.py failure_outcome, about line 149). A deploy or shutdown releases the job, does not count the release, and it is re-claimed (worker.py about lines 430-440). Each attempt builds a fresh RunBudget with run_spent=0, so a '3 USD per run' auto job can spend 3 USD × (attempts + releases). Fix: at attempt start, subtract this job_id's own ledger spend from the run cap: per_run_left = cap − SUM(cost) WHERE job_id = ctx.job_id. Record the attempt count in the result. Also do not rely only on 're-read the ledger before every paid post'. record_dfs_call_with_pool and record_dfs_call swallow write failures (shared/dfs_client/call_log.py:166-167, 189-190), and record_dfs_call_sync writes on a background thread (:193-215), so the ledger lags or undercounts. Enforce month = (ledger at attempt start) + the in-memory charges of this attempt, and make a failed cost-log write of a paid call abort the run.

C4 (blocker, S6) D3 'treat an empty PAA list as missing' creates a repeat-buy loop. Today fresh_tour_ids keys on fetched_at only (s1_prefetch.py:177-184). That age check is what stops a tour whose SERP had no PAA box from being bought again. seed_serps already skips rows with empty PAA (:198-199). If [] counts as missing, every S1 prefetch or wave re-buys a live SERP (_tour_serp, :330-352) for each tour whose SERP really has no PAA. The design itself says the answer would be empty again, so the purchase repeats with no end. Fix: keep the fetched_at reuse. Add paa_source='none' (or paa_attempted_at, in migration 437) so an answered-but-empty SERP counts as fresh for cis.seo.research_serp_fresh_days. Only the $0 store derive may fill it in between.

C5 (blocker, S3/S7, the 25/09 shape) B3 and A3 step 4 let a tenant's Brand-tab market save start an automatic platform-wide purchase in a new market (every in-scope place, about 5,877, ≈1 USD). It is capped, but it is exactly 'a tenant action fans out platform-wide', which AA-646 forbids. The trigger is also wide: TARGET_MARKETS_SQL (research_coverage.py:39-44) counts every tenant with is_active AND cancelled_at IS NULL, so tenants with account_status lead, applied, trial, past_due or suspended count, and so do kind demo and internal (CHECKs at db-schema-reference.md:14233, 14237). A demo or E2E tenant could spend the month's money. If auto-activation is kept, (a) add a setting cis.seo.research_market_eligible_tenants (default: kind='agency' AND account_status='active'), applied in TARGET_MARKETS_SQL for research and activation; (b) define the activation cap as one total per run and at most one activation market per night; (c) count it inside the month cap (already stated).

C6 (blocker, S5) The 'new activity → needs_requalify' flag is not 'LLM re-propose only'. Today a requalified place is planned as stale in every requested market and in the SERP tier when its map is not reusable (segment_research.py:759-767: p.markets = list(market_codes)). Its new keywords are then bought in every target market. A stored flag set by segment_matching would also be set in bulk by an action-vocabulary change, a re-atomize wave or an S1 catalogue rerun. One night could then try to re-buy thousands of fresh places. Fix: order requalify places last, after never-researched and stale places. Add a per-run limit setting cis.seo.research_requalify_max_places (and a per-run share). When more places are flagged than the limit, report them in the panel and alert; do not buy them in the auto run. Correct the cost text: buying volume for new keywords in N markets, not ~$0.0001 per place.

The auto payload must set dfs_queue from a setting, cis.seo.research_auto_dfs_queue (default 'standard', maker_checker). Make the job refuse (NonRetryable) any created_by='system:auto' payload whose scope is missing or unknown. Make auto_new select only never-researched places.

S5 is not 'no migration'. needs_requalify is a pure function of the name and the map rows (segment_research_batch.py:362-374), not a column you can set. acp_contract.place_keyword does not store the actions its map was proposed from (columns: subject_kind, subject, keyword, rank, country, activity — country_activity rows only — source, prompt_version, jev_*, proposed_at; db-schema-reference.md:161-177). Detecting a new activity therefore needs a new column (proposed_actions text[] or a hash) plus a reader change in reusable_keywords.

The rename carry is unsafe. _SEGMENT_UPSERT_SQL can relabel a Segment to a DIFFERENT real place (segment_matching.py:868-877; AA-857 relabelled 'Delhi' to a Taiwan hotel). canonical_place text is also shared by many Segments. Copying segment_research_log + place_keyword would mark another place fresh with the wrong keywords, and a copied map that is fresh by log skips the plain-keyword check in reusable_keywords (batch :356-357). Limit the carry to proven same-entity merges (atom_segment_alias chain, place dedupe job), or drop it: the volume store already makes a rename cost only the LLM proposal plus one SERP.

B1 research market set is incomplete. A proxy reads proxy_of data, so the set must be: real declared markets ∪ proxy_of(declared proxy markets) ∪ platform default. Otherwise an NZ-only agency reads AU data that nobody keeps fresh once no agency declares AU. Also dedupe when an agency declares both UK and SG (SG reads UK).

Who drives spend. TARGET_MARKETS_SQL counts every tenant that is_active and not cancelled (research_coverage.py:39-44). That includes shared.tenants.kind 'demo'/'internal' and account_status 'lead'/'trial'. Most market declarations today come from test or demo tenants (about 11 tenant rows). 'Paying agency' therefore cannot be enforced as designed. Filter auto activation and the research set to kind='agency' AND account_status IN a Settings list (for example ['active'], with 'trial' optional, maker_checker).
